findings.description: The bucket is configured to be publicly accessible with no bucket ACL restricting access and no public access block, exposing its contents (including a customer master file) to anyone on the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored unencrypted, violating the principle that encryption at rest should be the default state for stored data.
The bucket has no logging block configured, so there is no audit trail of access to this (public) bucket, hindering detection of unauthorized access.
A customer master spreadsheet (likely containing PII) is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, preventing audit trail collection for access to sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, removing visibility into access patterns and potential misuse.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket despite storing data science datasets, leaving them unencrypted at rest.
